Purely additive: a new optional top-level property (required: [] at the schema root, per-item `required` is internal to the array's own object shape), never required at the document root -- no previously-valid coordinator.local.md becomes invalid. 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0 added the optional top-level `collaboration_mode` (enum solo|multi|auto) and `collaboration_bot_exclude` (array of strings) properties for coordinator/bin/collab-verdict.py (M0CDAGA-C5); same additive class, nothing required, no previously-valid document becomes invalid. The same 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0 bump also adds the optional top-level scalar `terminal_test_cmd` (type string; docs/plans/2026-09-11-repo-supplied-terminal-test-command-key.md C1). No BUMP_CLASS_VOCAB term exactly names a top-level scalar addition (`top-level-array-additive` is array-specific; the other terms describe nested fields, enum values, pattern widening, or major breaks), so x-bump-class takes the nearest-fit term on the safe side, `nested-field-additive`, which keeps the full reader-first / dual-gate discipline instead of the non-holding carve-out reserved for declared-tolerant array additions. No declared-tolerant consumer set is claimed, so the bump takes the bilateral-sequencing discipline, not the non-holding carve-out. Nothing becomes required at the document root, so no previously-valid coordinator.local.md becomes invalid. 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0 adds the optional top-level `post_ceremony_skills` array of skill-id strings, read by the /workweek-complete and /merging-to-main skill prose; same additive class, nothing required. 1.4.0 -> 1.5.0 adds the optional top-level scalar `design_registry_path` (type string, minLength 1), read by coordinator/hooks/scripts/_design_registry_gate.py; x-bump-class keeps its nearest-fit term as the 1.2.0 note reasons, and nothing becomes required. 1.5.0 -> 1.6.0 adds the optional per-target `app_session` validate fields (build, start, port, ready_path, ready_timeout_s, build_timeout_s, build_isolated, env, request_headers, routes, variants), read by the `app-session validate` verb's parse_validate_config (claude-klabauter coordinator_core/ops/_app_session_validate_contract.py); every typed leaf admits the string form the parser coerces, every level stays open, and nothing becomes required.
title: coordinator.local.md frontmatter
description: Repo-root coordinator.local.md frontmatter — committed per-repo doctrine config (not gitignored, not machine-local). Declares the KNOWN keys read by live consumers (coordinator/hooks/scripts/_posture.py, coordinator/skills/validate/SKILL.md's fast_test_cmd/full_test_cmd resolver, the ceremony post-command hook seam, coordinator:install's project_type/project_subtypes onboarding, and the human-facing-doc-staleness detector's doc-registry four). Every declared key degrades to a fleet default when absent or malformed at the reader, per each reader's own fail-open contract — this schema documents shape, not obligation; nothing here is `required`. `app_session` (docs/plans/2026-08-15-launch-half-to-engine-ops-and-skill-surface.md § Design) declares the PM-ruled per-target launch config shape, read by the app-session skill's launch verbs and by its `validate` verb (parse_validate_config). `terminal_test_cmd` (docs/plans/2026-09-11-repo-supplied-terminal-test-command-key.md) is likewise reader-less: it declares the shape only, and no reader consumes it yet.
_additionalProperties_note: Permissive by design, and load-bearing here specifically: this corpus has hit the closed-schema/no-slot failure three times in one day (sizing-object EM-settled, sizing-object boundary justification, verdict_cited), and 56 of the 68 schemas under coordinator/schemas/ are open or unset vs 12 closed (counted directly) -- open is the house norm, not the exception. additionalProperties is intentionally left unset (open) at every level of this schema, including inside app_session's per-target objects: an unrecognised top-level key, an unrecognised app_session target name, and an unrecognised per-target field must all validate. Do not add additionalProperties: false anywhere in this file.

engagement_posture.description: Per-repo override of the engagement-posture resolver's default rung. Read by coordinator/hooks/scripts/_posture.py:102 (_VALID_POSTURES at _posture.py:~40 enumerates exactly these three values); an unrecognised or absent value fails open through the ~/.claude/coordinator-identity.yaml rung to the hardcoded 'precision' default (_posture.py:11-15).

fast_test_cmd.description: The fast/day-to-day test command for this repo, run verbatim and unsanitized (argv resolved via shlex, not shell=True) by the /validate seam. Resolution order is env (COORDINATOR_FAST_TEST_CMD) -> this frontmatter key -> skip-with-notice (coordinator/skills/validate/SKILL.md:18-19); absence is a skip, not a failure, at ad hoc invocation, but fails loud at a cadence gate (FAST-TEST-CMD-MISSING-CHECK, DR-142).

full_test_cmd.description: The full/slow test command for this repo, same resolution and trust model as fast_test_cmd (coordinator/skills/validate/SKILL.md:18-19,26-28). May be identical to fast_test_cmd when a repo has no separate slow tier (a tiering choice, not a schema constraint).

project_type.description: Canonical project-type classification asked once during coordinator:install onboarding (DR-099). 'unreal-engine' marks an Unreal Engine repo: ue-territory review signals fire on every plan. Legacy values ('unreal', 'meta', 'web') are migrated away from, not accepted here.

project_subtypes.description: Optional free-form engine/stack-routing tags alongside project_type (e.g. 'unreal' for a game-dev repo). Free-form by design (DR-099) -- not a closed enum.

workday_start_post_command.description: Opt-in per-repo command run at the end of /workday-start, argv-only (no shell=True), advisory: always exits 0, one redacted prose summary line. First token must be a real executable on EVERY OS the repo is worked on -- pnpm/npm/npx/yarn are .cmd shims that CreateProcess cannot launch, so they resolve on macOS/Linux and are a silent WinError 2 on Windows; name the interpreter instead (node scripts/x.mjs). (coordinator/docs/wiki/ceremony-calibration/workday-workweek-cadence.md:87-92, and that page's Semantics section; ceremony-post-command hook seam, docs/plans/2026-07-08-ceremony-post-command-hook-seam.md).

workday_complete_post_command.description: Same seam as workday_start_post_command, fired at the end of /workday-complete (coordinator/docs/wiki/ceremony-calibration/workday-workweek-cadence.md:93).

workweek_start_post_command.description: Same seam as workday_start_post_command, fired at the end of /workweek-start (coordinator/docs/wiki/ceremony-calibration/workday-workweek-cadence.md:94).

workweek_complete_post_command.description: Same seam as workday_start_post_command, fired at the end of /workweek-complete (coordinator/docs/wiki/ceremony-calibration/workday-workweek-cadence.md:95).

human_facing_docs.description: Per-repo override of the human-facing-doc-staleness detector's tracked doc list, e.g. [README.md, INSTALL.md, CONTEXT.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, coordinator/README.md]. Engine-side fleet default applies when absent (docs/plans/2026-07-28-human-facing-doc-staleness-detector.md:429-444).

doc_staleness_commits.description: Commit-count staleness threshold for the doc-staleness detector (docs/plans/2026-07-28-human-facing-doc-staleness-detector.md:429-444).

doc_staleness_days.description: Day-count staleness threshold for the doc-staleness detector, paired with doc_staleness_commits (docs/plans/2026-07-28-human-facing-doc-staleness-detector.md:429-444).

doc_verify_ignore.description: Repo-level residual known-good-citation ignore list for the doc-staleness detector's content-verification leg (docs/plans/2026-07-28-human-facing-doc-staleness-detector.md:224,577). Distinct from the per-doc frontmatter key of the same name on an individual tracked doc; this is the coordinator.local.md-level list.

terminal_test_cmd.description: Repo-supplied test command for the terminal commit gate, run verbatim and unsanitized. Optional; absence means the gate falls back to its default. Reader-less: the shape is declared here before any reader consumes it.

collaboration_mode.description: Override of the collaboration detector (coordinator/bin/collab-verdict.py), read from the examined repo's own coordinator.local.md. `solo` forces mode solo (the only input that lowers a latched multi), `multi` forces multi, `auto` (default, also when absent) defers to commit-authorship detection.

collaboration_bot_exclude.description: Extra author emails the collaboration detector drops as bots, on top of `*[bot]` and `*@users.noreply.github.com`. A single key holding a list, never repeated keys.

name.description: Short identifier for this ceremony-cadence runner, e.g. 'hook-and-whoami-tests'.

cmd.description: The ceremony-cadence test command. Single-command shape -- no &&/;/pipe chaining -- the same rule fast_test_cmd and full_test_cmd carry (DR-088). Runs at ceremony cadence: never per-commit, never by a subagent (DR-088 Tier T ceiling), and gated per this repo's Build & Test tier classification for this key.

collection_roots.description: Repo-relative directories this cmd collects tests from. Consumed by coordinator/tests/guards/test_every_test_tree_is_collected.py to subtract this tier's coverage from its reachability walk -- parsed, never a hardcoded path constant in the guard.

known_red_count.description: Shrink-only count of pre-existing failing tests recorded at this tier's declaration. May only decrease as diagnosis chunks land; must never be silently raised.

ceremony_test_cmds.description: Named ceremony-cadence test runners distinct from fast_test_cmd/full_test_cmd -- for a tree that is real coverage but too expensive or cross-plane-dependent for the fast tier (docs/plans/2026-08-16-unstrand-the-hook-test-suite.md C8). Run at a ceremony gate's cadence, not per-commit; CLAUDE.md Build & Test cites this key rather than restating collection roots in prose.

post_ceremony_skills.description: Skill ids the /workweek-complete and /merging-to-main ceremonies invoke after their archive and merge steps, once per ceremony, advisory on failure. Absent or empty: no behaviour change. Contract: coordinator/docs/wiki/post-ceremony-skills.md.

design_registry_path.description: Repo-relative path of the design-registry instance, read by coordinator/hooks/scripts/_design_registry_gate.py. Absent: the default docs/design/registry.yaml.

name.description: Short identifier for this research pipeline, e.g. 'womens-journalism'. Named in the dispatch guard's deny reason.

spec.description: Repo-relative path to the Pipeline C spec the pipeline runs with: `/research` is invoked with this spec.

schema.description: Repo-relative path to the JSON Schema the pipeline's output files must conform to.

output_paths.description: Repo-relative directories or globs the pipeline writes. An Agent dispatch whose prompt names one (or its basename directory) is routed to Pipeline C.

subjects_hint.description: Optional keywords that identify this research (e.g. 'journalism', 'intel'). An Agent dispatch whose prompt contains one as a whole word is routed to Pipeline C.

research_pipelines.description: Repo-declared research pipelines. When present, the PreToolUse(Agent) guard coordinator/hooks/scripts/guard-research-pipeline-dispatch.py denies an ad-hoc non-Pipeline-C Agent dispatch whose prompt names a declared output path or subjects_hint keyword, and points the EM at `/research` with the pipeline's spec. Absent or unreadable: the guard allows silently.

app_session.description: PM-ruled per-target launch-lifecycle config (docs/plans/2026-08-15-launch-half-to-engine-ops-and-skill-surface.md § Design, 'PM-ruled config shape'). A mapping of target name (e.g. 'desktop') -> per-target object. C4 wired the engine-backed reader and the app-session skill to this shape; the `app-session validate` verb reads the build/start/port/routes/variants fields. additionalProperties stays open at this level: an unrecognised target name must still validate.

additionalProperties.description: Per-target launch config. `runtime` is the discriminator selecting how the target is resolved and launched (e.g. 'electron' resolves via the Electron npm-package convention; an unrecognised or absent runtime degrades to a plain argv command with no resolution step -- see § Design's 'runtime axis'). Runtime-specific fields (e.g. `command`) are additive per runtime and intentionally left open here rather than enumerated per-runtime, since Electron is the first implemented resolver, not the capability's definition.

runtime.description: The runtime discriminator for this target, e.g. 'electron'. Unrecognised or absent values fall back to a plain argv command (§ Design's 'runtime axis') -- this key is intentionally NOT a closed enum, since new runtime resolvers are expected to be added without a schema bump.

command.description: Argv-only launch command for this target (e.g. 'pnpm dev'). Spawned unsanitized, never via shell=True -- no shell=True path or shell-word-form compatibility shim is permitted for this seam (docs/plans/2026-08-15-launch-half-to-engine-ops-and-skill-surface.md § Design, 'Argv-only, no shell=True').

build.description: `app-session validate`: argv build command run before start (e.g. 'pnpm build'). The reader parses block mappings only.

start.description: `app-session validate`: argv command that serves the built app (e.g. 'pnpm start').

port.description: `app-session validate`: port the started app listens on. A digit string is coerced by the parser.

ready_path.description: `app-session validate`: path polled until the app answers; must start with '/'.

ready_timeout_s.description: `app-session validate`: seconds to wait for ready_path. A digit string is coerced.

build_timeout_s.description: `app-session validate`: seconds allowed for the build. A digit string is coerced.

build_isolated.description: `app-session validate`: build in an isolated copy. The parser reads true/false words from a string.

env.description: `app-session validate`: environment for build and start. Block mapping only; the parser coerces every scalar to a string.

request_headers.description: `app-session validate`: headers sent with every route request. Block mapping only; the parser coerces every scalar to a string.

routes.description: `app-session validate`: route name -> path, or -> {path, expect_status}. Block mapping only; never a list.

variants.description: `app-session validate`: variant name -> {env} overlay merged over env. Block mapping only.
